page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g9a.8xlarge is a general-purpose virtual instance based on KVM virtualization and the x86_64 architecture. Compute capability is delivered via 32 dedicated vCPUs from an AMD EPYC 9T25 processor clocked at 2.7 GHz. System memory totals 128.0 GB, establishing a standard 1:4 core-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

Network performance is specified at a 16 Gbps baseline bandwidth. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage, requiring external cloud block storage for operating system and application data. It features zero GPU accelerators and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, avoiding overhead from extraneous hardware subsystems.

The 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio provides resource balance for horizontally scalable enterprise applications that do not demand dedicated local NVMe arrays or GPU offloading. Qualitative cost efficiency stems from matching balanced compute and memory capacity directly to enterprise workloads. Target workloads include relational and document databases, enterprise backend services, container nodes, CI/CD pipeline agents, and batch data processing.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g9a.8xlarge is an x86_64 general-purpose instance powered by a 2.7 GHz AMD EPYC 9T25 processor under the KVM hypervisor. It is configured with 32 dedicated vCPUs and 128.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Network throughput operates at a 16 Gbps baseline. The server contains no integrated local storage volumes and no discrete graphics processing units, requiring external network block storage for operating system and application data persistence. By offering a balanced core-to-memory distribution without overhead from bundled accelerators or local storage disks, the instance provides steady resource efficiency for general compute environments. Suitable workloads include container orchestration nodes, backend web application clusters, enterprise resource planning services, relational database management systems, and distributed CI/CD build environments.
